locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages sockets? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. Every path out of probeRelay goes through finish(): reply, unexpected reply, oversized reply, error, close, and timeout. finish is guarded by settled, clears the timer and calls socket.destroy(), so the descriptor is released exactly once even when connect hangs or the peer never replies. The 'close' and 'error' handlers stay attached, so a late error after destroy cannot become an unhandled 'error' event.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A relay accepts the TCP connection but never replies. What happens?
choices: The probe hangs until the OS TCP keepalive gives up
The socket is closed by the peer, so the probe resolves via the 'close' handler
After timeoutMs the timer calls finish, which destroys the socket and resolves with healthy: false
The promise rejects with a timeout error that sweep must catch
choiceQuestions.explanation: setTimeout fires finish({ healthy: false, error: 'timeout ...' }), which destroys the socket. No keepalive is involved, the peer did not close anything, and the promise only ever resolves, never rejects.

choiceQuestions.prompt: After finish() calls socket.destroy(), the 'close' event fires. What effect does it have?
choices: None: settled is already true, so the second finish call returns immediately
It resolves the promise a second time with 'closed before reply'
It overwrites the healthy result with an unhealthy one in the registry
It throws because the socket is already destroyed
choiceQuestions.explanation: finish returns early when settled is true. A promise can only settle once anyway, markHealth runs on the single resolved value in sweep, and nothing throws on close of a destroyed socket.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With 200 relays and maxConcurrentProbes = 10, how many sockets can be open at once during a sweep?
choices: 200, because Promise.all starts all probes immediately
At most 10, because 10 workers each await one probe before taking the next endpoint
At most 1, because the workers share the next counter
It is unbounded if overlapping sweeps start from setInterval
choiceQuestions.explanation: sweep spawns min(10, 200) workers, each awaiting probeRelay before pulling the next index, so at most 10 probes are in flight. Promise.all is over the workers, not the endpoints; the shared counter distributes work rather than serializing it; and the sweeping flag makes overlapping sweeps return early.
